page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized cloud server instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM allocation per vCPU. Built on x86_64 architecture using an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, it consists of 1 physical core supporting 2 threads with dedicated CPU allocation. Cache specifications include 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. This instance type contains no integrated GPU accelerators and offers no local NVMe storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU throughput, reaching 2923.78 on stress-ng single-core tests. However, overall multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics reflect hardware limits inherent to a single physical core, placing multi-core CPU score and uncached memory bandwidth in lower performance tiers. Single-threaded text decompression and compression tasks show average performance, while specialized database and compilation scores remain low.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides qualitative resource efficiency for memory-sensitive execution environments that do not require extensive parallel processing power. Tradeoffs include limited multi-core concurrency and lack of included block storage. This instance is best suited for lightweight caching services, memory-bound single-threaded applications, and small-scale data processing workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized server powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core and 16.0 GB of RAM. The instance provides dedicated CPU allocation, 32 MB of L3 cache, and a high 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio, while lacking bundled local storage and GPU hardware. Benchmarks highlight strong single-core CPU execution, paired with average text generation and decompression rates. Conversely, multi-threaded performance, uncached memory bandwidth, and database transaction throughput fall into lower tiers due to the single physical core footprint. This server offers cost-effective memory density for workloads requiring significant RAM with modest parallel processing demands, making it well fitted for lightweight caching layers, single-threaded batch processing, and memory-bound background tasks.
